CORAM : MANGESH S. PATIL, J.

DATE : 16.01.2019 P.C. :
 Accused no.1 from Crime No. 315 of 2018 registered with Nilanga Police Station, Latur for the offences punishable under Section 188, 272, 273, 328 read with Section 34 of the I.P.C. and under Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 is seeking bail.
2.

Shortly stated the prosecution case is to the effect that several bags of Gutkha were found stocked in the house owned by accused no.2 who happens to be the father in law of the applicant, who is shown as accused no.1.
The articles were seized, the matter was reported and the crime was registered.
The applicant was arrested on 05.12.2018 and is now seeking bail.

sentences.text: The learned advocate for the applicant submits that the applicant no.2 to whom the house belongs from where the Muddemal was seized has been granted bail by the learned Additional Sessions ::: Uploaded on - 17/01/2019 ::: Downloaded on - 18/01/2019 06:52:3  2 31 ba 5.19.odt Judge.
The case of the applicant cannot be distinguished rather he stands on a better footing.
This Court has granted ad interim anticipatory bail to the co-accused which shows that they have not been absconding.

The entire Muddemaal has already been recovered,
samples have been taken and the report of the Chemical Analysis is awaited.
It is under these cirucmstances, presence of the applicant behind the bar is not necessary for completing the investigation.
There are no criminal antecedents reported.
The offence is not punishbale up to death or life imprisonment.
Even there is a serious doubt about the applicability of Section 328 of the I.P.C.
In the facts and circumstances of the case the applicant may be granted bail subject to to usual terms and conditions.
4. The learned A.P.P. opposes the application.
He submits that at this juncture the facts cannot be scrutinised to ascertain as to if Section 328 of the I.P.C. is applicable or not.
The offence is punishable up to ten years of imprisonment.
Gutkha is banned in the State.
The applicant was found in possession of a huge stock of Gutkha.
The investigation is still in progress and therefore releasing the applicant on bail is likely to hamper the investigation and the application may be rejected.

sentences.text: I have carefully gone through the papers.

Going by the allegations there is absolutely no whisper about the applicant having ::: Uploaded on - 17/01/2019 ::: Downloaded on - 18/01/2019 06:52:35 :
 3 31 ba 5.19.o administered or caused to administer Gutkha to anybody albeit it is assumed that he was possessing it, which is a necessary concommitant for constituting offence punishable under Section 328 of the I.P.C.
Besides, even according to the prosecution the stock had been found in the house which belonged to accused no.2 who is father in law of the applicant.
The applicant is being implicated because he was present in the house.

The father in law has been granted bail by the learned Additional Sessions Judge and as has been rightly submitted by the learned advocate the applicant stands on a better footing as compared to his father in law since the house belongs to the father in law.
6. Apart from the above state of affairs, the entire stock has already been seized.
The samples have been taken and forwarded for Chemical Analysis.
It is under these cirucmstances, one cannot comprehend as to how further detention of the applicant would facilitate further investigatoin.
The offences is not punishable up to death or life imprisonment.
The applicant deserves to be granted bail on merits as well as on the ground of parity.

Hence I pass the following or- der:
 ORDER  I) The application is allowed.
 II) The applicant be released on bail on executing a personal Ankush S/O. Nagnath Patil vs The State Of Maharashtra on 16 January, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142978231/
3 recognizance for an amount of Rs.25,000/- and on furnishing a solvent surety in the like amount subject to the 4 31 ba 5.19.odt following conditions:
a) He shall attend the concerned police station as and when called by the Investigating Officer till filing of the charge-sheet and shall co-operate him.
b) He shall not tamper the evidence or influence the witnesses.
III) Bail before the lower Court.
IV) It is made clear that the observations made herein-above are only prima facie and confined to the decision of this application and the trial Judge shall not feel influenced by them.
